author: robob27
body:
<!-- HOW TO USE: Under each "#### Heading" below, enter information relevant to your pull request.
Leave the headings unless they don't apply to your PR.

Please read carefully and don't delete the comments delimited by "< !--" and "-- >"
Once a pull request is submitted automatic stylistic and consistency checks will be performed on the PR's changes.
The results of these can be either seen under the "Files changed" section of a PR or in the check's details.

NOTE: Please grant permission for repository maintainers to edit your PR.  It is EXTREMELY common for PRs to be held up due to trivial changes being requested and the author being unavailable to make them. -->

#### Summary
Features "Add spell effect to remove fields, artifact with spell to remove fd_fatigue fields and lab room to spawn artifact with the remove_field spell"
<!-- This section should consist of exactly one line, edit the one above.
Category must be one of these: Features, Content, Interface, Mods, Balance, Bugfixes, Performance, Infrastructure, Build, I18N. Or replace the whole line with just the word None for no changelog entry.
For more on the meaning of each category, see:
https://github.com/CleverRaven/Cataclysm-DDA/blob/master/doc/CHANGELOG_GUIDELINES.md
If approved and merged, your summary will be added to the project changelog:
https://github.com/CleverRaven/Cataclysm-DDA/blob/master/data/changelog.txt -->

#### Purpose of change
Primarily attempting to re-add the ability to remove `fd_fatigue` fields (odd ripple, swirling air, tear in reality) that was added in #26226 and removed in #42971. I got really excited when my friend showed me a merged PR that made it possible to close a tear in reality, but sad that it seemingly got removed due artifact code being messy at the time. I thought it would be fun to try to find a somewhat interesting way to bring it back using spell effects while also making it possible to create spells that remove fields of any specified type.
<!-- With a few sentences, describe your reasons for making this change.  If it relates to an existing issue, you can link it with a # followed by the GitHub issue number, like #1234.  If your pull request *fully* resolves an issue, include the word "Fix" or "Fixes" before the issue number, like: Fixes #1234.
If there is no related issue, explain here what issue, feature, or other concern you are addressing.  If this is a bugfix, include steps to reproduce the original bug, so your fix can be verified. -->

#### Describe the solution
- Add a new spell effect `remove_field` that removes an `effect_str` field within aoe range.
- Uses this effect to create an artifact that can remove fields of type `fd_fatigue`.
- There is room for spells to have special handling based on the type of field removed.
- Using this, removing a `fd_fatigue` field causes negative effects on the player depending on field intensity:
    - Odd Ripple = 1 hour teleglow
    - Swirling Air = 5 hour teleglow
    - Tear in Reality = Random teleport, 10.5 hour teleglow (to get half an hour of the worst effects), 10 damage to all limbs
- Adds "portalmancy" relic procgen data. Currently contains only the newly added `altered_exposed_wiring_prototype` with the `remove_field`/`fd_fatigue` effect. This was done to lock the max charges to 1 and recharge type to none for artifacts with this type of power so that it didn't become something you could do all the time once you find an artifact with this power.
- Adds a new microlab room based on the existing altered object containment room with a guaranteed tear in reality and a 50% chance to spawn the new artifact and the following additional differences:
    - scattered slime blobs on the ground 
    - nether monsters instead of lab monsters
- The messages for the various fd_fatigue fields closing are based on player sight.
- Adds a debug menu option under spawning to spawn an artifact from the portalmancy relic procgen. I added this for ease of spawning the artifact for testing. Probably the existing "Spawn Artifact" option should prompt for which procgen group to use, but I felt like this was outside the scope of this PR. I could remove the new debug option now if it shouldn't stay.
<!-- How does the feature work, or how does this fix a bug?  The easier you make your solution to understand, the faster it can get merged. -->

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
- ~~Maybe the artifact should be a different type of object. I'm not terribly creative.~~ Updated to "exposed-wiring prototype".
- Maybe the containment room should be more original? It just seems so perfect for this too.
- Should there be a flag that allows removal of all fields of matching type in range instead of just the first found in the `area_expander`?
- Are the negative effects not enough/too much? Closing a tear in reality seems like pretty much guaranteed hounds. I was leaning on the side of "not enough because messing with a tear in reality should be super dangerous" and thinking maybe there could be some chance to have hallucinations permanently after seeing indescribable things in the tear in reality before it ejects you but figured I'd submit as is for feedback before taking it further.

<!-- Explain any alternative solutions, different approaches, or possibilities you've considered using to solve the same problem. -->

#### Testing

<!-- Describe what steps you took to test that this PR resolved the bug or added the feature, and what tests you performed to make sure it didn't cause any regressions.  Also include testing suggestions for reviewers and maintainers. -->
- Spawn 3x `altered_exposed_wiring_prototype` with `remove_effect`/`fd_fatigue` spell with the debug menu option
- Use map editor to create 3 `fd_fatigue` fields with all 3 intensities
- Use each `altered_exposed_wiring_prototype` to close one of the `fd_fatigue` fields. There should be a different message for each. The tear in reality should teleport you, damage you and add an intense/long lasting teleglow effect (get ready for the hounds).
- Set the ID of the new lab room to something you can easily spawn using nested mapgen in debug menu
- Verify that the artifact doesn't spawn every time and that the tear in reality is present
- Test with and without being able to see the various intensity levels, the messages will vary based on whether the player can see the field tile.
- Note: it seems like spawning a nested mapgen chunk doesn't update the map cache or something until you save and reload, which causes unexpected results when trying to spawn the room and immediately close the portal. If I spawn the room and attempt to close the tear without save/quit, it does not close. If I spawn the room, save/quit, reload the save and then close the tear, it will close. All tears spawned with "edit field" in the map editor always close as expected without any save/quit/reload.

#### Additional context
I tried to balance this in such a way that closing a tear in reality is not common and comes with a lot of danger. This is also my first time working with pretty much everything involved in this PR and the most c++ I've ever written. Please let me know if I'm missing anything even if it seems super obvious and apologies in advance for anything silly.
<!-- Add any other context (such as mock-ups, proof of concepts or screenshots) about the feature or bugfix here. -->

- Order comments by id instead of created_at

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14875032/146982912-4afef6f8-cd26-4e8a-b1e3-1c15e4577b05.png)

author: chengxiong-ruan
body:
Fixes #68031

Previously we only try to create constraint for shard column if
it's newly created. We check duplicate constraint for shard
column when `Alter Primary Key` and `Create Index`, however the
check is simply a name check. This pr adds logic to check
equivalent constraint by checking if the formatted expression
string is the same. With this logic we can try to create the
constraint no matter if a shard column is newly created or not.
With this fix, we also don't need to expose the constraint through
`SHOW CREATE TABLE` result since we make sure the constraint is
created or skipped if one already exists.

Release note (sql change): Before this change, the check constraint
on shard column used by hash sharded index was printed in the
corresponding `SHOW CREATE TABLE`. The constraint had been shown
because cockroach lacked logic to ensure that shard columns which
are part of hash sharded indexs always have the check constraint
which the optimizer relies on to achieve properly optimized plans
on hash sharded indexes. We no longer display this constraint in
`SHOW CREATE TABLE` as it is now implied by the `USING HASH` clause
on the relevant index.
